findings.title: Rejected device is cached before the DB write, so it bypasses the limit on its next request
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` (line 87) before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (line 93). When the limit is reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which `TagDevice` now returns (line 147) and `Anonymous.Authenticate` turns into an auth failure (client.go:45-46). The cache entry stays, though. The cache is created with a 29-minute TTL (line 42). On the same device's next request within that window, `localCache.Get(key)` hits (line 83) and `tagDeviceUI` returns nil. `Authenticate` then succeeds and issues an anonymous identity. So a device over the limit is rejected once and let in on every retry for 29 minutes. The same cache-first order also means a transient DB error in the new synchronous path blocks tagging for 29 minutes. Fix: write to the cache only after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds. The new tests don't catch this because none of them calls `TagDevice` with a limit set.

findings.title: Device tagging now runs synchronously on the request path
findings.body: The old code tagged in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and a panic recover. Now `TagDevice` runs inline with the request `ctx`, so an uncached device adds a COUNT query (when `device_limit > 0`) plus an INSERT/UPDATE to the latency of its first request. Every anonymous request from a device not yet in the 29-minute local cache pays this cost. Making it synchronous is needed to reject over the limit. Still, a request-context cancellation or DB timeout now surfaces as a tagging failure, and the panic recovery is gone. If sync is intended only for the limit, consider keeping the async path when `device_limit` is 0.

findings.title: Limit error is a plain error: no explicit status or log level
findings.body: `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is a bare `fmt.Errorf` (database.go:18), not an `errutil` error. In `authnimpl/service.go:356-364`, `errorLogFunc` only picks a log level for `errutil.Error`, so every rejection is logged at Warn with 'Failed to authenticate request'. The contexthandler stores it on `LookupTokenErr` (contexthandler.go:124) with no status mapping. A user rejected by the limit probably gets a generic 401 or 500 with no message saying the device limit was reached. Consider an `errutil` error with an explicit status, a message and a low log level.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic, and the update path can mis-report
findings.body: The limit check (COUNT at line 110, INSERT at lines 120-153) is not in one transaction. Concurrent first requests from several new devices on one or more instances can all see `count < limit` and all insert, so the limit is a soft cap. Separately, `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever `RowsAffected()==0` (line 95). On MySQL, `RowsAffected` counts changed rows, not matched ones (unless the driver sets clientFoundRows). An update that sets identical ip, user-agent and second-precision `updated_at` would then be reported as 'limit reached' for a device that exists. Consider doing the check atomically, or at least document the soft limit.

findings.title: The 30-day expiration is now defined three times
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceExpiration` is declared in anonstore/database.go:16 and again in anonimpl/api/api.go:18. `thirtyDays` in anonimpl/impl.go:25 still has the same value. Export one constant from `anonstore` and reuse it. Also, `pkg/server/wire.go:374-375` still registers `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and binds `AnonStore`. The provider now needs an `int64` that wire cannot supply, and `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` builds the store itself. Both lines are stale and should be removed.

findings.title: Limit tests don't cover the main behaviours
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only covers rejection of a new device once the limit is hit. It does not cover: an existing device still being updated at the limit (the `updateDevice` success path); an existing device older than 30 days being refused; or `TagDevice` and `Anonymous.Authenticate` returning an error and then continuing to fail on a repeat request. That last case would have exposed the cache bug in impl.go:87. There is also no test for `device_limit` parsing in setting.go.

findings.title: New `device_limit` option is not documented in the ini files
findings.body: `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` is read here, but `conf/defaults.ini` (line 581) and `conf/sample.ini` (line 570) have no entry for it. Administrators won't find the option, and 0 meaning 'unlimited' is not stated anywhere. Add the option with a comment to both files.

findings.title: The default is `undefined`, but the backend always sends a number
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` makes the class field's inferred type `undefined`, while `GrafanaConfig` declares `number | undefined`. The backend DTO (`frontend_settings.go:195`) is a non-omitempty `int64`, so the frontend receives `0` for 'no limit', never `undefined`. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined`, or use `0`, so it matches what is actually sent. The value is also not read anywhere in this PR.

contracts.action: Anonymous.Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously and fails authentication on ErrDeviceLimitReached
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous goroutine in the same function, which tagged with a 2-minute background context and only logged errors
contracts.before_after: Before: fire-and-forget, never affected the auth result. After: inline on the request ctx. ErrDeviceLimitReached returns (nil, err). Other errors are logged at Warn and auth still succeeds. Authnimpl then joins the error and tries the next client (service.go:207-209), and contexthandler stores it in LookupTokenErr (contexthandler.go:124).
contracts.visible_effect: A new device over the limit is rejected on its first request. Because of the pre-write cache entry in tagDeviceUI, it is accepted on the next request within 29 minutes.
contracts.failure_mode: The local cache is set before the DB write (impl.go:87), so a rejected device is cached and let through on retry. A request-ctx cancel or DB error is logged and the device is untagged for 29 minutes.

contracts.action: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts recent devices and falls back to updateDevice at the limit
contracts.equivalent_path: The unconditional upsert (lines 120-153), still used when deviceLimit is 0
contracts.before_after: The upsert is unchanged. The new branch adds a COUNT, with no transaction around the count and the write.
contracts.visible_effect: At or over the limit, only existing devices updated in the last 30 days are refreshed. Others get ErrDeviceLimitReached.
contracts.failure_mode: Concurrent new devices can overshoot. MySQL RowsAffected==0 can occur for an unchanged row.

summary:
The PR adds a configurable anonymous device limit. One blocker: `tagDeviceUI` writes the local cache before the DB write, so a device rejected by the limit is let in on its next request for 29 minutes (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87). Smaller items:

- The limit error is a plain `fmt.Errorf` with no explicit status or log level.
- Tagging now runs on the request path.
- The count-then-insert is not atomic.
- The 30-day constant is defined in three places.
- `wire.go` still has stale `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` entries.
- The new `device_limit` option is missing from `defaults.ini` and `sample.ini`.
- Test coverage is thin.
- The frontend default `undefined` doesn't match the `0` the backend sends.
